messages:
kai: Heads up — planning to land a tiny TF change in staging: rename Service port on `inference-api` from `grpc` -> `grpc-inference` so it matches our HTTPRoute/backendRef port name. Quick sanity check before I push: will this break routing or trigger LB recreation?

sasha: Why rename? if backendRef uses port name it needs to match, otherwise route will stop matching. If your HTTPRoute references port name (not number) then yes traffic will drop.

matt: This should not recreate ALB/NLB itself unless the k8s Service annotations or type change. Port name renames are an in-place patch AFAIK, but the controller that translates to AWS target groups may update target group attributes if it uses port name in health check config. Recommend staging test.

kai: Good point — our HTTPRoute uses `backendRef: port: name: grpc-inference` (we added that in the canary config). TF diff only touches the `kubernetes_service` resource ports block, nothing else in LB module. I pasted the diff: ```diff
-  port {
-    name = "grpc"
-    port = 8010
-    target_port = 8010
-  }
+  port {
+    name = "grpc-inference"
+    port = 8010
+    target_port = 8010
+  }
```

jordan: If you rename the port on the Service, existing PodEndpoints don't change. But Gateway controllers reconcile HTTPRoute -> Service by name/port; if the HTTPRoute expects `grpc-inference` but Service still has `grpc` then the route will fail to attach, causing 404s. So sequence: update Service first, then HTTPRoute, or do both in same rollout.

sasha: For zero-downtime: do a two-step canary — add the new port name in Service (keep old name too if k8s supports multiple ports on same container) or create duplicate port entry with same port number + new name for a short window. Then update HTTPRoute to point to new name, verify sessions, then remove old name.

matt: Agree. You can temporarily add both ports like: ```yaml
ports:
- name: grpc
  port: 8010
  targetPort: 8010
- name: grpc-inference
  port: 8010
  targetPort: 8010
``` That prevents route breakup. AWS target groups don't care about port name — they use port number — but Gateway API matching does.

infra-bot: FYI: altering `ports[].name` in `kubernetes_service` will produce a `kubectl apply` patch; Terraform state will reflect no LB replacement. No AWS resource replacement detected in plan.

kai: Good to know. One more: our ALB TLS secret is bound at the Gateway level (secret `prod/gw-cert`). Will this change touch TLS?

jordan: No — TLS termination is Gateway-level. Port name changes on the backend won't affect certs. Only worry is healthcheck path/port configured by ingress controller annotations if those derive from port name (uncommon).

sasha: Quick checklist before merge: 1) Apply dual-port Service in staging 2) Patch HTTPRoute to new name and verify 3) Smoke GRPC traffic + stream stability (grpc-web tests) 4) Remove old port name after 10m of clean metrics

kai: I'll do the dual-port approach in staging and open a tiny follow-up PR to switch prod with the same sequence. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412 — contains k8s svc snippet and TF change. If anyone wants to review quickly that would be great. :pray:

matt: LGTM — can approve once staging pass is green. Also ping on call if you plan prod roll at 2am — we'll watch ALB target group health. :eyes:

kai: Thanks all — will follow the checklist and report back.
